In this discourse, Nietzsche
disassociates himself finally from the
higher men, and by the symbol of the
lion, wishes to convey to us that he has
won over and mastered the best and the
most terrible in nature.
That great power and tenderness are kin,
was already his belief in 1875--eight

when the birds and the lion come to him,
it is because he is the embodiment of
the two qualities.
